newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- More than 55,000 people gathered in Hong Kong's Victoria Park to commemorate the Beijing massacre in 1989. The organizer vowed that the vigil would not be the last.
-- MING PAO -- Three hundred students of the University of Hong Kong confronted the police after the University resisted letting them place the Pillar of Shame statue in the campus.

-- MING PAO -- The English-language Hongkong Standard was raided by the Independent Commission Against Corruption which was investigating an alleged scheme to inflate the paper's circulation figures to attract advertisers.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Sources said some red-chip companies were actively preparing to inject investments and seek listings. They hoped that when new mainland regulations on red chips come out, these red chips can be judged by old regulations because most of their work were done before the new guidelines come out.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Because of the surge in the property and stock markets, the licence fee for stock brokers has gone up tremendously. Last week, a broker paid $5.8 million to get a licence, representing a 21 percent increase from April.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- The Villa Esplanada residential project by China Resources, Cheung Kong and Sun Hung Kai Properties set a record as the number of applications to buy flats in the Tsing Yi Island project was 200 times the number of flats available.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese scientists said pandas have a low reproduction rate because many female pandas have endocrinopathy problems which make it difficult for them to get pregnant.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Securities and Futures Commission was planning a ground-breaking code of practice for the territory's US$150 billion fund management industry.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- According to a report commissioned by the government, a proposed overhaul of the Companies Ordinance could lure businesses back to Hong Kong to incorporate from locations such as the British Virgin Islands.
